original_question: Is it true that the extension of the A. Agrachev–R. Gamkrelidze construction of groups from pre-Lie rings in(J. Soviet Math., 17(1981), 1650–1675) suggested in Definition 66 of(A. Smoktunowicz, J. Pure Appl. Algebra, 229, no. 12(2025), 108128) produces groups from pre-Lie rings? If this extended construction does give a group, then it also gives a brace, and so an affirmative answer to this question would have consequences for the theory of set-theoretic solutions of the Yang–Baxter equation and for the theory of braces.
target_in_paper: Problem 21.123 in the 21st edition of the Kourovka Notebook; this is the notebook formulation of the open question raised by Smoktunowicz’s 2025 paper on the generalized group-of-flows construction for finite pre-Lie rings.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the official target: it identifies the precise 2025 Smoktunowicz paper, the extension of the Agrachev–Gamkrelidze group-of-flows construction, the central yes/no issue ('does it really produce groups?'), and the stated consequence that a positive answer would also produce braces and thus matter for set-theoretic Yang–Baxter theory.
missing_details: The nearest official formulation is not the older brace/pre-Lie correspondence problem 20.92, but the newer Problem 21.123 of the 21st Kourovka edition.
The paper does not ask this for arbitrary pre-Lie rings; the construction is set up for finite pre-Lie rings of cardinality p^n, with p a prime and n a natural number.
The nearby context imposes the technical assumptions called Properties 1′ and 1″ on the pre-Lie ring; equivalently, the ring satisfies Property 3 in the paper’s later notation.

The construction at issue is the paper’s generalized group-of-flows operation from Definition 66 of the published article (the accessible web preview exposes the same construction under earlier numbering).
The paper proves only that this construction yields a pseudobrace; the open point is whether the multiplicative operation is actually a group law.

The draft does not explicitly say that the additive group is unchanged; this matters because, if the multiplicative law is a group law, then the same underlying set with the original addition becomes a brace.
The quantifier should be universal: the question is whether every pre-Lie ring satisfying the paper’s hypotheses gives a group under the generalized construction.
refined_question: Let A be a finite pre-Lie ring of cardinality p^n, where p is a prime, and assume that A satisfies the technical hypotheses called Properties 1′ and 1″ in A. Smoktunowicz, 'An extension of the group of flows method for finite pre-Lie rings' (equivalently, Property 3 in the paper’s later notation). If one applies to A the generalized group-of-flows construction defined in Definition 66 of that paper—the extension of the classical Agrachev–Gamkrelidze construction obtained by replacing the classical division-by-p step by the paper’s pullback/division maps—does one always obtain a genuine group law on A? Equivalently at the level intended in Kourovka Problem 21.123: is the pseudobrace produced by this generalized construction always in fact a brace with the same additive group as A?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Kourovka Problem 21.123, so that is the exact target. It should not be replaced by the broader older problem 20.92 about bijective correspondences between F_p-braces and pre-Lie algebras. The 2025 paper’s introduction explains that the new construction extends the Agrachev–Gamkrelidze group-of-flows method, states Theorem 1 proving only a pseudobrace, and then explicitly asks whether the construction is actually a group. The same introduction also states that if the construction does give a group, then it gives a brace with the original addition, which is exactly why the Yang–Baxter/braces consequence belongs in the refined version. What your draft was missing are the paper-faithful scope restrictions: finite cardinality p^n and the standing assumptions Properties 1′ and 1″/Property 3.
